name: Petrochemical Industry
description: Iran’s petrochemical industry uses natural gas and petroleum-derived feedstocks to manufacture chemicals and industrial materials. Understanding its performance requires distinguishing installed capacity, aggregate production, and products available for sale. [s1][s2]

seo.title: Iran’s Petrochemical Industry: Feedstocks, Production and Constraints
seo.description: Explore Iran’s petrochemical industry through its gas supply, production measures, product mix and documented evidence gaps.

content.heading: From hydrocarbons to industrial materials
content.content:
Petrochemicals connect oil and gas extraction with chemical manufacturing. A feedstock is material transformed into another product; fuel supplies energy for that transformation. The distinction matters because a petrochemical complex can require natural gas in both roles. The U.S. Energy Information Administration identifies petroleum products and natural gas as feedstocks for Iran’s petrochemical production. [s1]

This makes the industry different from a simple extension of crude-oil exports. Evaluating it requires asking what materials enter a plant, what products leave it, and which further manufacturing stages occur inside Iran. Iran Open Data’s analysis identifies a concentration in basic chemicals and limited downstream processing as structural weaknesses. That is an interpretation of the industry’s product mix, rather than proof that every producer has the same business model. [s2]

content.heading: Large gas resources do not guarantee continuous supply
content.content:
Iran’s gas resources must serve competing demands. EIA describes seasonal pressure from heating and electricity generation, inadequate storage, and investment and technology constraints affecting upstream development. Its assessment explains why a country with substantial reserves can still experience industrial supply shortages. Reserves describe a resource underground; reliable plant deliveries depend on production, processing, transport and demand management. [s1]

EIA also identifies gas capture and processing projects intended partly to supply petrochemical users. Such projects should be read as dated development descriptions: an announced commissioning date does not establish that a facility was completed or delivered its intended feedstock. [s1]

content.heading: Reading production figures carefully
content.content:
Iran Open Data reports lower aggregate production in Solar Hijri 1403 than in 1402, despite rising nameplate capacity. It separately discusses marketable products, demonstrating why those measures should not be substituted for one another. The accompanying table preserves its approximate production figures and original reporting years. [s2]

The underlying National Petrochemical Company and Statistical Center tables were not inspected directly. Consequently, these observations are a secondary-source transcription with unresolved coverage and aggregation questions. They establish a reported decline, but do not support a precise calculation of plant efficiency or domestic value added. [s2]

content.heading: A dated account of disruption
content.content: The August 2026 Iran Open Data article reports conflict-related damage to petrochemical utilities and infrastructure around Mahshahr and South Pars. It explicitly acknowledges the absence of a comprehensive production-capacity damage assessment. This supports identifying disruption as a research priority, but does not establish which facilities had resumed operations by the editorial cutoff. A current industry assessment therefore needs verified plant-level operating reports alongside comparable production statistics. [s2]

name: Heavy Industry
description: Iran’s heavy industry includes steelmaking, nonferrous metals and mineral-based building materials. These activities connect extraction and processing with energy infrastructure, freight transport and further manufacturing. [s1][s2][s3]

seo.title: Heavy Industry in Iran: Steel, Metals and Mineral Processing
seo.description: Understand Iran’s heavy industries, their production chains, energy dependencies and a verified five-year direct-reduced iron series.

content.heading: An interconnected industrial system
content.content:
Heavy industry is best understood through connected production stages rather than a single national output total. Iran’s mineral industries encompass iron and steel, copper, aluminum, cement and other processed materials. The U.S. Geological Survey’s country report distinguishes production, facilities, trade and government oversight, each of which answers a different question about industrial development. [s1]

The Ministry of Industry, Mine, and Trade oversees the mineral sector. USGS also describes substantial government control of large mineral companies through the Iranian Mines and Mining Industries Development and Renovation Organization, usually abbreviated IMIDRO. These sector-level descriptions do not establish the ownership or management arrangements of every individual enterprise. [s1]

content.heading: Ironmaking, steelmaking and finishing
content.content:
Direct-reduced iron, or DRI, is an intermediate material in steel production. Mobarakeh’s technical description illustrates one Iranian production chain: iron-bearing materials arrive by rail, pellets are prepared, and gases produced from methane remove oxygen from the iron oxide. The resulting sponge iron proceeds to steelmaking. This example also shows how an industrial complex depends on mines and transport systems beyond its own boundaries. [s3]

Finishing adds another set of distinctions. Rolling and surface treatment produce materials with different dimensions, properties and applications. AIST’s account of work at Mobarakeh documents investment in pickling, acid regeneration and other processing equipment. Growth in crude material output and improvements in finishing capability are therefore separate developments; one should not be used as automatic evidence of the other. [s4]

content.title: Iran’s direct-reduced iron production, 2021–2025
content.y_axis_label: Million metric tonnes of direct-reduced iron
content.interpretation: The published series rises in every year shown. It measures an ironmaking intermediate, so it must not be read as finished steel output, sales or installed capacity. [s2]

content.heading: What the production series establishes
content.content:
The five annual observations provide a consistent view of one important industrial process. They do not represent the whole heavy-industry economy. Copper, aluminum and cement require their own indicators, and adding their physical tonnages to ironmaking output would not produce a meaningful measure of industrial value. [s1][s2]

A similar distinction applies within steelmaking. Worldsteel publishes crude steel, direct-reduced iron, finished-product use and trade as separate indicators. Comparisons should follow those definitions rather than treating every steel-related tonne as interchangeable. The chart is therefore evidence of a particular production trend, not a ranking of the performance of Iran’s industrial branches. [s2]

content.heading: Infrastructure changes the meaning of capacity
content.content:
Industrial capability depends on dependable energy as well as installed equipment. EIA’s 2024 assessment describes recurring electricity shortages affecting industrial users. That evidence cautions against treating a plant’s design capacity as its expected annual production. A facility may have machinery capable of a stated throughput while operating fewer hours because essential services are unavailable. [s5]

The same caution applies to expansion announcements. AIST’s historical account provides a documented example of processing lines reaching startup, which is a more specific milestone than an investment proposal. Even startup, however, does not establish sustained output or independently verified environmental performance over subsequent years. [s4]

For readers exploring the sector, the useful questions are concrete: which processing stage is being measured, where are its inputs obtained, and does the evidence describe installed equipment or actual operation? This framework connects the individual company and commodity pages without assuming that all heavy industries share the same production model. Current operating conditions, resource use and regional impacts still require additional evidence before this overview is ready for publication.

name: Mobarakeh Steel Company
description: Mobarakeh Steel Company is an Iranian steel producer whose technical documentation describes an integrated chain from ironmaking to rolled and coated sheet. Its manufacturing activities include direct reduction and the processing of cold-rolled, galvanized and tin-coated products. [s2][s3]

seo.title: Mobarakeh Steel Company: Ironmaking, Sheet and Coated Products
seo.description: Explore Mobarakeh’s documented manufacturing chain, its processing technology and the limits of available operating evidence.

content.heading: Understanding the production chain
content.content:
Mobarakeh’s technical documentation describes a manufacturing system extending from raw-material handling through ironmaking and sheet processing. Its ironmaking section identifies rail deliveries from mining areas in Kerman, Yazd and Razavi Khorasan provinces. This connects the complex to a broader supply network rather than a single nearby source of ore. [s2]

The company’s own descriptions are useful evidence of its production model, but they are not an independent operating audit. They should also be distinguished from group-wide statistics: the corporate website separately identifies group companies, so a consolidated total should not automatically be attributed to one plant. [s1]

content.heading: Making sponge iron
content.content:
Pelletizing prepares iron-bearing material for the reduction stage. Mobarakeh describes mixing fine materials and binders, forming pellets, and hardening them before direct reduction. In that next stage, gases made from methane react with oxygen in the pellets. The product is sponge iron, also called direct-reduced iron, which is transferred onward to steelmaking. [s2]

This sequence explains why ore supplies and natural gas are both significant inputs. It also prevents a common misunderstanding: sponge-iron tonnage is an intermediate output, not a measure of finished sheet supplied to customers. The company describes several linked units; their individual capacities cannot simply be added to calculate final production. [s2]

content.heading: Why finishing matters
content.content:
Cold rolling reduces the thickness of steel strip and changes its mechanical properties. Mobarakeh’s cold-rolling description explains a sequence involving surface preparation, rolling, cleaning and heat treatment. Pickling removes oxide scale from hot-rolled material; annealing helps obtain the properties needed for subsequent forming and finishing. [s3]

Coating creates further product distinctions. The documented product families include galvanized, tin-coated and prepainted material. These are different processing routes rather than consecutive steps that every coil must follow. A useful account of the company therefore needs more than a total tonnage: product specifications and the division between rolled and coated output also matter. [s3]

content.summary: This simplified diagram follows selected routes in the company’s technical description. Arrows indicate material processing, not ownership or reporting relationships; the diagram omits other finishing operations and does not establish current line availability.

content.heading: A documented processing investment
content.content:
An October 2006 AIST report records the startup of Techint processing lines at Mobarakeh, including pickling and acid-regeneration equipment. The account also describes work on electric furnaces and hot-strip-mill equipment. It provides a dated example of investment across several stages of the manufacturing chain. [s4]

The report includes supplier claims about process and environmental benefits. Those claims should remain attributed: a project announcement does not substitute for measured emissions, wastewater records or a later performance assessment. Likewise, historical startup confirms neither uninterrupted operation nor present capacity. [s4]

The supported picture is of a producer whose capabilities depend on linked preparation, reduction and finishing stages. A publication-ready contemporary profile still requires verified operating disclosures, a consistent annual production series and evidence on resource use and workforce outcomes.
